prompts.front: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: one square perspective cube-map face of an existing 360-degree can-recycling conveyor factory, for a high-detail 3D Gaussian Splat reconstruction. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and is a mathematically projected 100-degree-FOV view, NOT a loose style reference. Output one high-resolution 1:1 SQUARE image at native maximum fidelity (at least 1254 by 1254 pixels). Enhance photographic surface detail and sharpness ONLY. LOCK GEOMETRY: retain the exact camera, FOV, projection, horizon, object positions, sizes, straight lines, silhouettes, edge locations, exposure and neutral color balance of the input. Do not move, straighten, widen, resize, remove, duplicate or add any structural object. In particular do not crop, zoom or reframe. Preserve the outer 10 percent of the composition especially faithfully, since this face overlaps adjacent cube-map faces. The result should look like a sharper photograph captured from precisely the same fixed camera. Generate clean coherent microdetail inside the existing material surfaces, not merely contrast sharpening, oversharpen halos, painterly pseudo-detail or extra geometry. All foreground service-bay space stays empty. No robot, people, workbench, new conveyor, signage, logos, watermark or readable text. Keep the central double door, can bales on the left, blue baler on the right and every railing exactly in place. Add physically realistic fine seams, bolts, aluminum-can folds and metal texture within their existing silhouettes.

localizedEdits.front: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, one square 100-degree cube-map view of the existing can-recycling factory. Make ONE localized material/color change ONLY: the stacked rectangular bales of crushed aluminum beverage cans sitting on wooden pallets must become calm, neutral medium SILVER-GRAY compressed metal. Remove all bright colored can-label graphics and saturated red, green, blue, yellow and multicolor printing ONLY inside those stacked bale volumes. Keep believable compressed-can folds and subtle metallic crushed texture, but use a restrained monochrome gray palette with moderate low contrast, not glittery busy reflections. Preserve the exact bale outer silhouettes, number of bales, stacking arrangement, dimensions, position and wooden brown pallets. Everything OUTSIDE the stacked can bales is invariant: keep blue machines, colored loose cans on the conveyors, railings, doors, roof, concrete floor, yellow floor lines, lighting, camera, 100-degree FOV, perspective, framing and square canvas exactly unchanged. No crop, no zoom, no reframing, no geometry changes. Preserve the full high-detail native square resolution, at least1254 by1254 pixels. The goal is a subtle gray bale stack rather than a visually noisy multicolored pile. No added objects, text, signage, logos or watermark.
